en: Ask a client to sign the contract
Hello, the contract for "{name}" at {value} is ready. Please sign it before {start} so that we can start on time.
Hello, we start "{name}" on {start}. Please confirm that the site is clear and that we can have access that morning.
Hello, the defects period of "{name}" ends on {defects_end}. Please send us any defect you have found before that date.
Warn a client of a coming milestone
Hello, the milestone "{milestone}" of "{proj}" is due on {due}. We would like you to inspect it with us.
Hello, the milestone "{milestone}" of "{proj}" is {delay} days late. We are working on a catch-up plan and will send it today.
Ask for payment after a milestone
Hello, the milestone "{milestone}" of "{proj}" is complete. Please confirm it and release {amount}.
Ask a provider to renew cover
Hello, our cover for "{proj}" ends on {expiry}. Please send the renewal terms and premium this week.
Hello, our cover for "{proj}" ended on {expiry}. We need a renewal certificate urgently. Please call us.
Ask a supplier for a price
Hello, please send your current price for {item}, the delivery time and how long the price is valid.
Hello, your price for {item} rose to {price}. Can you hold the price for our tenders for the next 60 days?
Sample wording: adapt it to your country's law and your own practice.

We are pleased to submit our tender for this project. Our price is {col:tenders.bid}. It is based on the documents we received on {col:tenders.received} and on the assumptions and exclusions listed in our tender.
Our estimator for this tender is {col:tenders.estimator}. We confirm that the price stays valid for the period stated in the tender documents.
We would be glad to meet you to explain the price, the programme and the way we would organise the site.
To {col:tenders.client_name}. Project: {col:tenders.project}. The tender deadline is {col:tenders.deadline}.
While pricing this tender we found points in the drawings and the specification that need your answer. Please reply in writing so that every bidder has the same information.
We will list your answers in the assumptions of our tender. Please reply before the deadline so that we can finish our price in time.

We invite you to quote for this package using the drawings and the scope we send with this letter. Please state what your price includes and excludes, your programme and the days your quote stays valid.
We ask for your quote by {col:quotes.valid}. We compare the quotes for price, programme, experience and safety record.
Letter of intent to a subcontractor
We intend to place this package with you at your quoted price of {col:quotes.amount}, if we are awarded the contract. This letter is not an order. Please keep your price and your programme available.
We will send the subcontract for signature as soon as the client confirms the award.
Letter asking a client for feedback after a lost tender
Thank you for considering our tender. We understand that another contractor was chosen. We would be grateful if you could tell us where our price, programme or experience fell short.
Your feedback helps us improve our future tenders, and we would be happy to price your next project.
Thank you for inviting us to tender. After reviewing our current work and the time available, we must decline this time. We hope you will think of us for future projects.
We value our relationship with you and would be pleased to be invited again.
Notice of a site visit before tender
We ask for safe access to the site and for a person who can show us the boundaries, the existing services and the places for deliveries and cabins.
We will wear protective equipment and record what we see so that the price allows for the real site conditions.
Acceptance of contract and start of works

We accept the contract at the value of {col:contracts.value}, with a start on {col:contracts.start} and completion on {col:contracts.finish}. Retention is {col:contracts.ret_pct} and payment is due in {col:contracts.pay_days} days.
Delay damages are {col:contracts.ld_day} for each day, limited to {col:contracts.ld_max}. The defects period ends on {col:contracts.defects_end}.
Notice of a completed milestone and payment release
To the client of the contract. Project: {col:ms.proj}. Milestone: {col:ms.milestone}.

We confirm that the milestone was due on {col:ms.due}. It releases {col:ms.amount}, which is {col:ms.pct} of the contract value. Please confirm the milestone and release the payment within the payment days of the contract.
Request to renew a bond or insurance
The cover of {col:bonds.amount} ends on {col:bonds.expiry}. Please send the renewal terms and the premium so that the cover continues without a gap.
The contract stays in force and the client requires the cover to remain valid.

Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: overhead, profit, target and minimum margin, contingency, price rise, warning days and the score needed to bid.
Fill Clients and Client Contacts. Leads, tenders, wins, win rate and contract value for each client fill in from the other sheets.
Record every enquiry on Leads and score it on Bid Reviews. The decision compares the total with your pass mark.
Enter each tender on Tender Register with its deadline and price. Direct cost comes from Estimate Lines, then margin, days to the deadline and the status fill in.

Price a tender on Estimate Lines: choose the tender and cost code, then type the quantity and the rates for each unit. Keep standard rates on Unit Rate Library, Labour Rates, Material Prices and Plant Hire Rates.
Log every subcontractor quote on Subcontractor Quotes. Each quote is ranked inside its package and compared with the average.
Write what you found on Site Visits, price the dangers on Risks and Allowances, and state what the price leaves out on Exclusions.
When a tender is won, add it to Contract Register with value, retention, payment days, defects months and damages for each day late, then list its Contract Milestones and its Insurance and Bonds.
Record each lost tender on Lost Tenders with the reason and the winning price, and read Win Rate by Kind and Tender Months to see where you win.

Use the 14 calculators for the estimate, markup and margin, price check, overhead, unit rate, contingency, bid or no bid, cash-flow curve, retention, delay damages, price rises, win rate needed, quote levelling and the deadline plan.
Print 10 sheets and 10 letters, follow 10 step-by-step checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Estimating Dashboard and Charts every week: deadlines, tenders waiting, margins, win rate, quotes that ended, overdue milestones and bonds ending.
Project schedule, site diary and delay claims for every job you build
Schedule with finish dates that calculate
start and working days give the finish by WORKDAY, planned progress, days late and a status for every task of every project
Planned against actual progress for each project
task progress rolls up by working days to a project percent, the days ahead or behind and a flag
Daily site diary with labour cost
weather, workers, hours lost and work done for every site day, with the cost of the lost hours
Delay log with cost and claim position
each delay shows its cost from the contract value and whether you can claim it from the client
days claimed, days granted, money value and days waiting for every claim
wet days and lost days count themselves from the diary and show the days over the normal allowance
RFI tracker with working-day due dates
the due date uses working days; response days and overdue requests show at once
failed or missed inspections and expiring permits are flagged before they stop work
each job shows the crew and whether materials and plant are ready, so blocked jobs are known early
tasks that could move the finish show their float after the days already late
each milestone gives the payment value and the date the money should arrive
Crew plan by trade and month
workers planned against workers on site, with the labour cost and short crews flagged

One row for each project with client, manager and dates; planned and actual progress, delay days, the daily cost of delay and a schedule flag fill in from the tasks and diary.
Schedule: phases and tasks for every project
One row for each task with its start, working days, predecessor and percent done; the finish, planned progress, days late and a status fill in by themselves.
One row for each milestone with its planned and achieved dates and the share of the contract it releases; the value, state, days late and the payment date fill in.
Site diary: one entry for each project and day
One row for each site day with weather, workers, hours lost and the work done; the month, labour cost, the type of day and the client phone fill in.
One row for each delay event with its cause, days lost and who carries it; the cost of the delay and whether you can claim it from the client fill in.
One row for each claim with the days asked for, the days granted and the decision; the money value, the days waiting and the share granted fill in.
One row for each inspection with the authority, planned and actual date and the result; days to go, delay and the status fill in, so a failed or missed inspection stands out.
Look-ahead plan for the next three weeks
One row for each job planned in the next three weeks with the crew, subcontractor and whether materials and plant are ready; the week, days ahead and a Ready or Blocked flag fill in.
One row for each action agreed at a site meeting with owner, due date and priority; the status, days overdue and the owner phone fill in.
Requests for information and response days
One row for each request for information with the date raised and answered; the due date, response days and an on-time or overdue status fill in.
One row for each drawing with its latest revision, date and status; the age and a check that tells you when an old issue may still be in use fill in.
One row for each photo taken on site with the area, a description and who took it, so you can find progress, defect and delivery pictures later.
One row for each person who visits a site with company, purpose and hours; the month and a warning for visitors who had no safety induction fill in.
One row for each project and month with the wet days you normally allow; wet days, lost days and the days over the allowance count themselves from the site diary.
One row for each permit with authority, application date, expiry and fee; the days left and a Valid, Expiring soon or Expired status fill in.
One row for each setup item at the start of a project with owner and due date; the status and days overdue fill in so nothing is missed before work begins.
One row for each task that could delay the finish with its cause, float and action; the task, project, finish, progress and float left are looked up and counted from the schedule.
One row for each lesson with the cause, the days and cost it cost and who recorded it; the month and the cost for each day lost fill in.
One row for each project, month and trade with the workers planned and on site; the shortfall, labour cost and a Short crew flag fill in.
One row for each staff member and month with phone and role; tasks starting, actions due, requests raised and diary entries count themselves, and a workload flag shows who is overloaded.

Hello, an update on {name}: {actual} complete against {plan} planned. The planned finish is {finish}, {days_left} days from today.
Hello, {name} is {gap} against plan and we have logged {delay_days} delay days. We will send you a recovery plan this week.
Hello, {open_rfi} requests for information on {name} are waiting for an answer. Each late answer can delay the work. Can we clear them this week?
Hello, the planned finish of {name} is {finish}. We need your decisions and access on time to keep the date.
Hello, the work done on {name} to date is worth {earned}. We will send the progress claim for this value.
